firewall-first.statement: All web traffic is evaluated in the firewall module first, and only traffic that does not violate a firewall policy is forwarded to the web module.

quotes: All web traffic is first evaluated in the firewall module and only if it passes the firewall module

nonweb-firewall-only.statement: Outbound traffic to ports other than 80/443 (or other HTTP or HTTPS ports) goes directly to the firewall module and is blocked if it violates a firewall policy.

quotes: it sends the traffic directly to the firewall module for policy evaluation.

web-block-firewall-log-conflict.title: Does the firewall log show a web-module block as allowed or blocked
web-block-firewall-log-conflict.detail: The policy-enforcement guide says Firewall Insights shows traffic that passes the firewall but violates a web policy as allowed. Later, for HTTP traffic, it says that when the web module blocks a transaction the Public Service Edge does not send the traffic to the firewall module, 'However, your firewall logs show that the user's web transaction is blocked.' The two statements are in the same guide and are not reconciled.
web-block-firewall-log-conflict.blocks: using the firewall log action alone to tell a firewall block from a web block

quotes: However, your firewall logs show that the user's web transaction is blocked.

module-internal-order.title: Evaluation order among Filtering, NAT, DNS, IPS and FTP
module-internal-order.detail: The old reference asserted both a fixed sequence (Filtering, NAT, DNS, IPS, FTP) and, separately, that NAT Control evaluates before Firewall Filtering, and that a flow traverses all four with a block from any dropping it. No captured source states an order or a traversal rule among the firewall policies. The only ordering stated is that ATP rules evaluate before IPS Control rules.
module-internal-order.blocks: answering whether a NAT rewrite changes what Filtering sees

ztunnel-2-firewall.title: Whether Z-Tunnel 2.0 engages the firewall without an option
ztunnel-2-firewall.detail: The old reference said Z-Tunnel 2.0 forwarding engages the firewall automatically and that without the opt-in the firewall and IPS never run on Z-Tunnel 1.0 and PAC traffic. The captures only say the firewall must be enabled for Z-Tunnel 1.0 and PAC; they say nothing about Z-Tunnel 2.0.
ztunnel-2-firewall.blocks: explaining why firewall rules do or do not apply to a forwarding method
